title: The merge tool refuses a `--fix-check` record that drops an earlier Round line
why: Runner 10 via the coordinator 01:23 CST Nov 14 (relayed; the archive and the code lines are unread by triage): closed PR #1892 (archive/fix-check-round-lines, 11c2103e3dbf). On main, the merge/merge.py `--fix-check` branch (about lines 4567-4604) checks only the top round and a bad fix base, and `review_state` (merge.py:3655) reads only the last design-reviewer line, so a fix-check record can drop an earlier Round line unnoticed.
source: Runner 10 01:23 CST Nov 14 (relayed). Reusable from the archive: the small standalone `dropped_round_lines(last, rec)`. Owner item 741 (ruling own-741-a-lint-fix-no-r3) ruled out the old `round_floor` and net-value freeze edits, so the fresh lane writes none of those. Neighbour: fix-check-record-carries-rounds (todo: the record the tool prints carries the chain's round lines; the print side, this step is the refuse side); the lane says whether they fold.
note: Triage 01:31 CST Nov 14: the mistake the guard would stop: a fix-check record posted with an earlier Round line missing, so the chain reads shorter than it was. Fix: a fresh lane writes `ReviewFixKeepsRounds` cases red first on main (a record that drops an earlier Round line refuses; a record that keeps every line passes; the first fix check with no earlier lines passes), then builds from `dropped_round_lines`, with none of the old `round_floor` or freeze edits (owner item 741). A guard or check change: own lane, review rounds apply. Not started.
